author: BBC News
description:
Latino voters could decide which party controls Congress after November’s midterm elections. Two years ago, 48% of them voted for Donald Trump, a record for a Republican presidential candidate. But with fuel prices still high, and his immigration crackdown affecting families who have lived in the US for a long time, is that support slipping away?

Justin and Anthony discuss the campaign in Texas, where the Senate race is becoming a fight to win over Latino voters. Trump has mocked the Democratic candidate James Talarico for being vegan (though he isn’t), and Talarico has thrown down the gauntlet, challenging his Republican rival Ken Paxton to a TV debate on Fox News.

Justin then talks to Mike Madrid and Chuck Rocha, the Republican and Democratic strategists behind The Latino Vote podcast. They say Latino voters are angry, mostly about the economy. title: Could ‘angry’ Latino voters cost Trump the midterms? | BBC Americast

author: BBC News
description:
The latest polling suggests that Democrats have the edge in the upcoming midterm elections on November 3.

They hope they can flip seats in the House of Representatives and take control of the Senate. 

That would make life difficult for Donald Trump in his last two years in office, hampering his chances of passing legislation in Congress. 

The state of Iowa has voted for Donald Trump three times, but many voters are angry about rising prices and the war in Iran. 

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Sarah Smith in Iowa.

The Houthis in Yemen have attacked the presidential palace in the port city of Aden - the seat of the internationally-recognised government. 
 
Meanwhile, President Masoud Pezeshkian has told Iranians that the country is facing its most intense blockade since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, and has accused the US of seeking to provoke public protests.
 
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis says it has intercepted a missile in the Medina region. The Houthis have threatened more attacks on Saudi Arabia but have denied carrying out this one.
 
Finally, according to reports, the US is considering using its biggest non-nuclear bomb against Iran if President Donald Trump should decide to renew combat in the war that has hit a deadlock.

The BBC has identified 254 incidents in which the Israeli military has been accused of killing or injuring people that it said it was investigating but have had no public outcome.

description:
The jury in Russell Brand's rape trial won't see a TV documentary that a complainant says led her to come forward. 
 
Judge Mr Justice Bennathan said it would be unfair to show the Channel 4 Dispatches programme because the allegations it contains have not been tested in court, but said that jurors will hear about it during the trial. 
 
The 51-year-old actor and comedian faces seven charges - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.
 
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.

description:
Two security personnel have been killed in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally recognised government.
 
The prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace, but many others were injured, Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC.
 
Houthi-run media reported that the group had struck "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers" as well as weapons depots.
 
A coalition led by Saudi Arabia backs the government and is providing air support for an offensive by pro-government forces against the Iran-backed Houthis.

description:
Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said, as he accused the US of withdrawing crucial support.
 
He also accused the US of withdrawing intelligence-sharing on Russian strikes, and said restrictions to Starlink satellite services used by Ukraine's military were deliberate.
 
Ukraine's military relies on US early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks to mount air defences, limiting successful strikes, while Starlink internet links are used throughout its war effort to guide drones and protect its skies.
 
But on Tuesday night, Starlink suddenly and unexpectedly restricted the speed at which drones could fly while still maintaining internet connection. This disrupted some battlefield "missions", a top Ukrainian official said, and hampered Kyiv's ability to protect itself from incoming Russian attacks.

description:
At least 33 children and one teacher have been killed after a school roof collapsed in Pakistan, with hospitals saying the large majority are children under the age of 13.
 
Police have arrested the owner of the school and the structure of the building is being investigated.
 
Emergency services rushed to the private Al-Khair school in the Dir Colony neighbourhood from after 08:48 local time (04:48 BST).
 
Rescue workers and residents searched the rubble for hours, looking for more children who could be trapped.
 
In a statement, the office of Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari says "this heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock".

Iran has increased attacks on shipping in the vital Strait of Hormuz, as it changes tactics to increase pressure on the United States.
 
Two ships are reported to have sunk within 24 hours.
 
Separately, the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen say they have attacked the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's oil company, Aramco.
 
Severe food shortages have been reported in Yemen, by the UN, as the fighting continues to escalate.
 
And there are reports that Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu discussed new joint strikes on Iran, although both have said they don't favour any attacks before elections in their respective countries.
